passage: Bhai Ram Singh, born in 1858 in the village of Rasulnagar in Punjab, entered the Mayo School of Art in Lahore as a student of woodcarving and rose to become its principal, the first Indian to hold the post. His buildings, among them the Lahore Museum and parts of Aitchison College, combined Mughal and Sikh ornament with European planning. His best-known commission, however, lies far from Punjab. Invited to England in 1890 to decorate a new banqueting hall at Osborne House, Queen Victoria's residence on the Isle of Wight, ______ Every surface of the Durbar Room, as it came to be called, carries his designs.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: intricate plasterwork modeled on the ornament of Mughal and Sikh buildings was what Ram Singh used to cover the ceiling and walls.
choices.B: Ram Singh covered the ceiling and walls with intricate plasterwork modeled on the ornament of Mughal and Sikh buildings.
choices.C: the ceiling and walls were covered by Ram Singh with intricate plasterwork modeled on the ornament of Mughal and Sikh buildings.
choices.D: Ram Singh's intricate plasterwork, modeled on the ornament of Mughal and Sikh buildings, covered the ceiling and walls.

explanation.why: The sentence opens with the modifier "Invited to England in 1890 to decorate a new banqueting hall," which describes the person who was invited. The main clause must begin with that person, Ram Singh, as its subject. Only one choice does.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This makes "intricate plasterwork" the subject, so the modifier wrongly says that the plasterwork was invited to England.
explanation.B: Correct. "Ram Singh" is the subject right after the modifier, so it is he who was invited to England.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This makes "the ceiling and walls" the subject, so the modifier wrongly says that the ceiling and walls were invited to England.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This makes "Ram Singh's intricate plasterwork" the subject, so the modifier wrongly describes the plasterwork, not Ram Singh, as having been invited.
